gaps.note: Commercial break edit hides the immediate transition after the collection plate joke.

stage_a.note: Highly energetic and positive delivery throughout the pitch, smiling and moving.
Loud, passionate vocal delivery and dynamic gestures conveying strong excitement.
Friendly and approachable demeanor, warmly engaging with the guest demonstrators.

venture.description: An iOS app marketplace that allows users to book in-person experiential learning sessions with passionate experts.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 presents his experience marketplace app and introduces demonstrators.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: S5 asks F1 to share his background.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 details his career at Procter & Gamble.

turns.speaker: S6
turns.summary: S6 jokes with S1.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 explains the philosophy behind the besomebody movement.

turns.speaker: S6
turns.summary: S6 challenges F1 for talking too much without getting to the point.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 briefly acknowledges the challenge.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: S5 asks what the actual product is that customers buy.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 demonstrates the iOS app and how to book an experience.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: S2 asks about the typical fee for an experience.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 states they take a twenty percent cut of the fee.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: S3 asks how fast the platform can scale its supply side.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 deflects by citing the hashtag's global reach.

turns.speaker: S6
turns.summary: S6 asks if the hashtag usage translates to company revenue.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 claims he trademarked the hashtag.

turns.speaker: S6
turns.summary: S6 challenges that a trademark does not equal revenue.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 insists the company owns all assets associated with the brand.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: S5 expresses confusion about whether it is an activity or training platform.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 pivots to say strategic partnerships are their scaling method.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: S1 asks how the company protects itself against lawsuits.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 admits they haven't faced it yet but will figure it out.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: S2 presses for an answer on handling liability problems.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 claims they are raising capital to help insure themselves.

turns.speaker: S6
turns.summary: S6 asks how long they have been offering experiences.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 states they have operated for twelve months in Austin.

turns.speaker: S6
turns.summary: S6 asks if the platform is open to everybody yet.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 explains they decided to focus on scaling partnerships.

turns.speaker: S6
turns.summary: S6 asks for the booking revenue from the previous month.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 reveals they booked about two thousand dollars.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: S1 points out the contradiction in F1's liability insurance answers.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 clarifies that hosts must have their own liability insurance.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: S3 asks why a partner would grant exclusivity with no current users.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 explains the exclusivity is limited to their specific app.

turns.speaker: S6
turns.summary: S6 asks if the partner's revenue is entirely dependent on them.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 confirms the partner relies on them.

turns.speaker: S6
turns.summary: S6 asks if F1 guaranteed the partner any minimum revenue.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 states they did not guarantee minimums.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: S2 challenges that the partner will starve without minimums.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 attempts to defend the partner's situation.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: S2 interrupts to let F1 finish answering S6.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 explains they act as a payment platform for partners.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 changes the subject to show a motivational sign.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: S1 jokes about F1 bringing a collection plate.

turns.speaker: S6
turns.summary: S6 exits, citing the excessive backstory and preaching.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: S2 exits, finding F1 abrasive and unable to listen.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: S5 asks why the viral movement isn't translating to business growth.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 insists it is working but hasn't scaled yet.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: S5 exits, stating he doesn't understand the business.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: S4 exits, believing the app won't stand out in a crowded market.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: S1 asks how much of his own money F1 invested.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 states he has invested two hundred thousand dollars.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: S1 challenges F1's claim of pioneering experiential learning.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 deflects by citing the size of the education industry.

turns.speaker: S6
turns.summary: S6 criticizes F1 for continuing to preach.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: S1 exits due to unresolved concerns about liability protection.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 attempts to pivot the conversation to brand value and money.

turns.speaker: S6
turns.summary: S6 challenges F1 for believing his own nonsense.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 defends his work ethic and the community he built.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: S3 exits, noting F1 struck out with all the sharks.

decisions.note: The longer the backstory, the worse the deal, more preaching equals less money.
Finds him enormously abrasive, lacks capacity to listen.
BS antenna goes up, doesn't understand the business.
Too many apps out there, this won't make it.
Never got over how he will protect himself against liabilities.
Struck out on every one, zero.

claim_conflicts.note: F1 claims capital is for company insurance, then says hosts must have their own.

record.notes: The pitch involves multiple guest demonstrators. The founder uses highly energetic, almost preaching-style delivery which alienates the panel.
